newsitem.title: USA: APICS business outlook index fell to 49.1 in Oct.
newsitem.headline: APICS business outlook index fell to 49.1 in Oct.

text.p: The American Production and Inventory Control Society (APICS) business outlook index fell to 49.1 in October from 53.8 in September.
The current component declined to 47.7 from 53.6 in September, and the future component fell to 50.6 from 54.0
A reading of 50 indicates neutral sentiment, APICS said.

"The significant declines in shipments, new orders, and unfilled orders taken together suggest that the effect of higher interest rates on discretionary consumer spending and housing are now starting to take a toll on the manufacturing sector," said an APICS report.
The APICS index is compiled monthly from a survey of manufacturing firms and is calculated by averaging respondents' ratings of current and future conditions.
Three of four current components fell in October. Shipments dove to 53.0 from 63.3 the month before, current inventories fell to 42.4 from 51.8 and production declined to 50.2 from 56.0.
Only the employment measure rose, to 45.2 from 43.3. Lower manufacturing employment is expected to continue for the rest of the year, APICS said.
Three of four future components fell in October, APICS said. The new orders component fell to 50.5 from 56.9, unfilled orders fell to 45.7 from 51.7 and inventory/sales ratio fell to 51.1 from 53.6.
Only the production planning rose, to 55.1 from 54.0.
